subject: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding

Hi Maria —

Attaching our current redline (Redwood_Acme_MSA_redline_v3.pdf). We read your last set of comments and want to align on two discrete items so procurement can run the Order Form without delay:

1) Defense control vs. reimbursement: our commercial intent is to accept defend-and-control for third-party infringement claims limited to issues arising from Redwood-delivered code and model artifacts. For claims alleging customer prompt/usage‑generated infringement we proposed a reimbursement route in the Order Form.

2) Evidence & notice workflow: to speed triage, we propose a short checklist (see attached evidence-checklist.xlsx) and a single technical liaison per claim to avoid duplicate asks.

Goal: confirm whether Acme is comfortable with the narrow split above and, if so, we can incorporate the exact language from redline_v3 and hand to procurement for signature. If not, please call out the specific clause(s) and proposed alternate language.

Requested timeline: can we lock language by close of business Fri 10/22? Ben and Kimberly are looped for pricing/contract/legal tradeoffs.

Attachments: Redwood_Acme_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (PDF), evidence-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Sr. Legal Operations (on behalf of Commercial)
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Gomez <procurement@acmelabs.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding

Jonas —

Thanks for the redline and the checklist. A few notes from Acme Legal / Procurement after an initial read:

• Defense control: Acme is generally open to defend-and-control for software copyright/patent claims tied to Redwood-delivered components, but we need a stronger commitment around consent to settle and approval rights for any settlement that would bind Acme.

• Prompt/output claims: procurement would like a clearer concrete carveout for model‑output claims; their ask is that Redwood reimburse reasonable defense costs for such claims unless there is a demonstrable defect in Redwood’s model artifact.

• Insurance/escrow: Acme will push for a warranty/insurance waterfall and wants to understand whether Redwood is willing to add a limited escrow/holdback for high-severity claims (we've attached procurement questions).

I’ve attached our procurement questions for your team (acme_procurement_questions.docx). I'll be out of the office Thursday morning — Luis from procurement will coordinate timelines.

Can Kimberly propose final clause language?

—Maria
Maria Gomez
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Acme Labs

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 12:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding

On Wed, Oct 21, 2026 at 10:04 AM Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com> wrote:
> Jonas —
> 
> Thanks for the redline and the checklist. A few notes from Acme Legal / Procurement after an initial read:
> 
> • Defense control: Acme is generally open to defend-and-control ...

Maria / Jonas —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Below are concrete edits I recommend we accept and where I want to push back. I’ll put redline language into the PDF if you want to see tracked changes quickly.

1) Settlement approvals: Redwood is willing to accept defend-and-control, provided Acme has reasonable approval rights over settlements that create ongoing obligations or monetary payments. Proposed language (short form): "Redwood shall not enter into any settlement that (a) imposes a permanent obligation on Customer, or (b) includes any admission of liability by Customer, without Customer’s prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld."

2) Model-output carveout: We can accept a reimbursement approach for claims based solely on customer-provided prompts or outputs. Proposed language (short form): "Claims arising from Customer-provided inputs or outputs generated by Customer prompts are excluded from Redwood’s defend-and-control obligation; Redwood will reimburse reasonable defense costs for such excluded claims if the claim is not caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct."

3) Insurance/escrow: Redwood cannot agree to a full escrow of model weights; we can discuss limited holdbacks tied to high-severity incidents or increase insurance limits for the specific deal. Suggest adding a 90‑day evidence preservation requirement (see attached evidence-checklist.xlsx).

If Acme accepts (1) and (2) above with the settlement approval carve, we can move language into the Order Form appendix and proceed to procurement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: evidence-checklist.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding

Maria / Kimberly / Jonas —

Short commercial note from Sales: we can accept the split Kimberly proposes, but to keep procurement moving we should offer a one‑time protection: if a covered third-party claim triggers a final judgment or settlement > $250k, Redwood will (a) assume defense control and (b) provide a credit equal to 25% of the first $250k of settlement/award against the first 6 months of hosting fees. That’s our compromise to reduce Acme’s expected net exposure while keeping overall unit economics intact.

If that sounds reasonable, I’ll flag it in the Order Form and ask procurement to push the DocuSign package.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmelabs.com>, Luis Gomez <procurement@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme MSA — third-party claim coverage: redline coordination & evidence onboarding

Thanks everyone — quick recap and next steps so procurement can close this week:

• Agreed draft positions: Redwood defend-and-control for Redwood-delivered code/artifacts; reimbursement for prompt/output-only claims (with exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct). Settlement consent language as proposed by Kimberly.

• Commercial compromise: Ben’s credit construct (25% credit up to $250k against hosting) will be included in the Order Form as a one-time protection; legal to capture the commitment in the Order Form billing appendix.

• Evidence & retention: Acme and Redwood will follow the attached evidence checklist. Redwood to preserve relevant logs/evidence for 90 days after notice; Acme to identify a single technical claim liaison for triage.

• Timeline: Kim/Redwood legal to post final clause language into the redline PDF today; Acme procurement to route DocuSign by COB Fri 10/22. Jonas will coordinate final check and confirm when DocuSign is live.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/packaging/ACME-2026-01/offer (working link)
